properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 25 at 7:36PM CST by NWS Bismarck ND
properties.description:
Patchy fog will reduce visibility to one quarter mile or less in
parts of south central North Dakota this evening. Motorists
should be prepared for rapidly changing conditions and use extra
caution traveling. Use low beam headlights and be extra cautious
at intersections and railroad crossings. The fog may also deposit
a thin layer of ice on elevated and untreated surfaces.

Conditions are expected to improve after midnight.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 25 at 8:22PM EST until November 25 at 9:15PM EST by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Central Craven County in eastern North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 915 PM EST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways. Overflowing poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 822 PM EST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is already occurring in the
advisory area. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain has fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
New Bern, Havelock, James City, Trent Woods, Riverdale, Croatan,
Coastal Carolina Regional Airport and Neuse Forest.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT UNTIL 915 PM EST THIS EVENING

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southwestern Carteret County in eastern North Carolina...
Southeastern Craven County in eastern North Carolina...
Southeastern Jones County in eastern North Carolina...
Onslow County in eastern North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 915 PM EST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the advisory area.
Between 1.5 and 2.5 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Jacksonville, Havelock, Morehead City, Newport, Harkers Island,
Piney Green, Camp Lejeune Center, Pumpkin Center, New River
Station, Stella, Swansboro, Hubert, Cape Carteret, North River,
Straits, Smyrna, Marshallberg, Pine Knoll Shores, Harlowe and
Silverdale.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 25 at 3:14PM PST until November 25 at 7:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves large
breaking waves up to 25 feet. Surf may worsen coastal flooding
along exposed beaches.. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High
astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low lying areas
around Humboldt Bay. Up to 1 foot of saltwater inundation above
ground level is possible near shorelines and tidal waterways.
Between 9.5 and 9.8 feet MLLW at the North Spit tide gauge is
predicted.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM PST this evening.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 8 AM to 3 PM PST Thursday.
High tide is at 12:54PM at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide
gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before
and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay
including parks and roads with only isolated closures
expected. Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in
the Arcata Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon. Dangerous
surf conditions and localized beach erosion. Beachcombing is
highly discouraged!.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The water levels from this event will be
higher than normal but not quite as high as the previous near
record recording from Tuesday 11/24 at 10.16 feet.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

predicted.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM PST this evening.

gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before
and after high tide.

including parks and roads with only isolated closures
expected. Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in
the Arcata Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon. Dangerous
surf conditions and localized beach erosion. Beachcombing is
highly discouraged!.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The water levels from this event will be
higher than normal but not quite as high as the previous near
record recording from Tuesday 11/24 at 10.16 feet.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 25 at 2:14PM PST until November 28 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding. For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking
waves of 15 to 22 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High
Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to 15 feet with
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until 3 AM PST Thursday. For
the Coastal Flood Warning, until noon PST Thursday. For the
High Surf Advisory, from 3 AM Thursday to noon PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beaches (especially Oceano Dunes,
Pismo Beach, Morro Bay, and Guadalupe Dunes), roads, and
structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful
waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of
ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers
(including Cayucos, Avila, and Pismo) and jetties. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Large breaking
waves may impact Morro Bay Harbor. Extremely high tides may
cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas
inside of harbor areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An extreme high tide of 7.8 feet will peak
between 9 AM and 11 AM Thursday morning.
properties.instruction:
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other water side
infrastructure.

properties.headline: High Wind Warning issued November 25 at 12:28PM PST until November 26 at 7:00AM PST by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...South winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 60 mph expected
for beaches and headlands.

* WHERE...In Oregon, Clatsop County Coast and Tillamook County Coast.
In Washington, South Washington Coast.

* WHEN...From 10 PM this evening to 7 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds will blow down trees and power lines. Some
power outages are expected. Travel will be difficult for high
profile vehicles.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The period of strongest winds are expected to
occur between 3-7 AM PST Thursday. Although it will be windy for
inland coastal communities, maximum gusts will be relatively weaker
compared to beaches and headlands with gusts up to 50-55 mph.
properties.instruction:
A High Wind Warning for the coastal headlands and beaches means a
hazardous high wind event is expected or occurring in those areas
along the immediate coast. Many of the headland areas and beaches are
vulnerable to very strong wind gusts that may pose a safety hazard
for individuals or high profile vehicles. The strong winds may also
cause property and/or tree damage. Sustained wind speeds of at least
40 mph or gusts of 58 mph or more are expected in those areas.
Coastal headlands are characterized by high, rocky shores and steep
sea cliffs.

Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.
